paragraphs: A signal that this suits experience is liking to turn drawings into measurable physical results, being willing to check dimensions, fits and clearances, and re-analysing after finding an error. Interest cannot replace machine tool training and on-site permission.

First judge whether you can tolerate fine machining, repeated measuring, standing and workshop noise. United States occupational material notes that some roles involve nights, weekends or overtime; the specific shift system must be checked with the target employer.

When choosing a direction, look at the output first: new moulds and tooling emphasise processes and assembly, while repair emphasises locating defects and testing; machine repair and forging production are adjacent occupations, and the responsibilities must not be conflated.

The low-cost experience uses this page's original fixture locating pin paper prompt. Check the drawing version, the upper and lower size limits and the inspection conditions, then revise the conclusions under the new E2 material. There is no need to buy tools, start machine tools or use real customer drawings for a trial.
Are you willing to check repeatedly for a reliable fit result?

Tool and die making suits people willing to read drawings, calculate, machine and check assembly results. An observable signal is recording the datum and tolerance and, when an anomaly is found, stating the basis rather than declaring acceptance by feel; at the same time, on-site safety training and the division of duties must be accepted.

This is an editorially designed experience pre-screen. A paper prompt can only reveal your thinking and recording habits, and cannot prove that you already have machine tool operating, precision assembly or independent release ability.

A more specific signal is: you confirm the drawing version and units first and turn the size requirements into upper and lower limits; you keep the original record of inconsistent readings and are willing to check the measuring instruments and the inspection conditions; when assembly jams, you locate the cause before proposing a handling suggestion. Rather than aiming to be fast once, being able to keep the basis consistently, carry out feedback and re-check the changes is more worth observing.

Signals that call for caution include treating machining experience as a reason to skip drawings and inspection, grinding randomly when a fit problem appears, or concealing out-of-tolerance results and missing inspection conditions to meet a delivery date. If repeated measuring, the workshop environment or the shift system clearly do not suit you, check the specific direction first; a single label of "good with your hands" cannot replace judgements about safety, precision and cooperation.

When finished, compare the E1 and E2 records: which conclusions changed because of the version or the valid readings, and which remain awaiting confirmation for lack of assembly inspection. Then judge whether you are willing to learn drawing reading and measuring, and look for supervised formal training.

The United States identity on this page is O*NET-SOC 51-4111.00. The objects are the making and repair of moulds, cutting tools, jigs, gauges and related tools; general part machining, machine maintenance and forging production each have their own task scope, and not every workshop role can be merged into this occupation.

For whether dimensions meet the requirements, check the drawing version, units, datum and tolerance first, then the measuring instruments and inspection records. The upper and lower limits of different versions cannot be mixed; readings whose inspection conditions cannot be confirmed count only as information awaiting re-checking.

For whether the process is reasonable, the shape, material, dimensions and surface requirements need to be linked, explaining the order of machining, assembly and testing. Confirm the technical requirements first, and let people with the corresponding authority choose the equipment and machining conditions.

New making, repair and modification have different task scopes. Record the tool to be delivered this time, the parts to be handled and the acceptance requirements; the fact that one part meets its dimensions does not mean the whole mould is ready for production.

When assembly or testing shows jamming, clearance or a defective part, go back to the corresponding structure and size requirements to locate the cause. Do not change the datum, tolerance or critical fit without confirmation, and after adjustment the affected items need to be re-inspected.
When communicating with design, machining, inspection and production staff, state the drawing version, the anomaly location, the measurement basis and the items awaiting confirmation.

Work quality depends on precision, equipment conditions and reliable records. O*NET notes contexts such as hazardous equipment, noise and standing; the actual environment and protection follow the role, and working hours cannot be inferred for everyone from an occupational summary.

At delivery, keep the drawing and process versions, the critical dimensions, the assembly inspection and test results, and the unresolved problems. Measuring, mould trials and release are confirmed by the actual chain of responsibility, and completing the machining cannot replace all acceptance.

The following are two editorial processes arranged from the official tasks: new moulds and tooling turn technical requirements into an inspectable tool; repair and modification locate the problem first and then use re-inspection to show whether the handling worked. The processes vary with the tool type and the workshop's division of duties.
New moulds and tooling
Check the drawing and material → plan the process → machine the parts → fit and assemble → inspect and test → record and deliver
The mould, cutting tool, jig or gauge made to the technical requirements, together with its inspection records
Repair and modification
Receive the anomaly material → locate the wear or failure → confirm the repair plan → handle the parts → re-inspect and test → record the changes
The repaired or modified tool, the re-inspection results and a statement of the unresolved problems
Shared professional foundation
Drawing reading · tolerance calculation · materials and processes · machine tool work · fitting and assembly · inspection and testing
Where is the boundary between tool making and general part machining?

Both read drawings, use machine tools and check dimensions. This occupation looks further at the structural fit and function of moulds, jigs, gauges and tools; general part machining focuses on delivering the workpiece as required. Actual roles may overlap, and the judgement should still be made by object, acceptance and responsibility.
Core purpose
Making, repairing or modifying tools used for machining, locating, forming and inspection, so that the related parts meet the technical requirements and work in the agreed way.
Machining material into the parts or workpieces required by the drawing, with dimensions, shape and surface requirements as the corresponding delivery basis.
Main objects and basis
Moulds, cutting tools, jigs, gauges and their parts; based on drawings, models, material requirements, assembly relationships and test objectives.
Blanks and parts to be machined; based on the corresponding drawings, processes, equipment and inspection requirements.
Core process
Calculate dimensions and tolerances, arrange the process, machine the parts, fit and assemble, check the tool and carry out the necessary tests.
Set up and operate equipment for the specific process, machine the workpiece, monitor the process and verify the requirements of the finished product.
Main outputs
The tool or mould that meets the agreed dimensions, fit and functional requirements, plus inspection, test and repair records.
The machined parts meeting the corresponding drawing requirements and the process inspection records; it is not inferred from this that the whole tooling is acceptable.
Responsible party

The maker is responsible for the authorised machining, fitting and inspection tasks, while design changes, on-site safety and delivery release are confirmed according to the actual division of duties; the occupational title does not grant every operating authority.
Machinists complete the assigned equipment and process tasks, and the process, inspection and production supervisors confirm the related results according to the organisation's duties.
How they cooperate
Working together on design, part machining, assembly and testing, communicating dimensional deviations, tool status and the impact of modifications.
Working together on the process, tooling, equipment status and part inspection, and reporting anomalies to the corresponding responsible person.
Delivery boundaries
One acceptable part does not mean the mould's or tooling's function and testing have all passed.
Part machining ability does not automatically equal mould assembly, repair, mould trial or technical change ability; the task scope needs separate verification.
Six occupational judgements that require a basis

The questions below are an editorial self-check based on this occupation's tasks. State the drawing, record or test basis first, then raise the items to be checked; do not treat the paper analysis as on-site operating instructions.
Have the technical requirements and the process order been confirmed before machining?
Are the version and the inspection conditions used for the current dimensional judgement consistent?
Where did the assembly or test anomaly occur, and which items will the change affect?
Does the material selection meet the tool's conditions of use?

Check the material type, hardness or heat resistance and the records against the requirements; where information is missing, hand it to the technical responsible person for confirmation, and do not replace the material basis with appearance or experience.
Are the test conditions and the on-site operating scope clear?

Confirm the test objective, equipment, protection and responsible personnel, and follow the workshop's process; the learner's paper practice does not include real mould trials, lifting, welding or machine tool operation.
Can the delivery material explain the results and the problems that remain unresolved?

Preparation｜drawing reading and dimensional calculation｜Check the drawing, model and technical requirements, calculate dimensions, shape and tolerances, and plan the machining sequence for the tool or mould.

Machining｜material and equipment selection｜According to the material properties and the dimensional and surface requirements, choose the corresponding metals, tools and equipment and complete the authorised setup preparation.
Machining｜cutting and forming｜Set up and operate conventional or CNC machine tools to turn, mill, grind and drill the parts so that they approach the specified dimensions and surface requirements.
Assembly｜fitting and tool assembly｜Dress, adjust and fit the related parts, and make, repair or modify moulds, jigs, gauges and other tools.

Re-checking｜dimensional and functional inspection｜Use measuring instruments to check dimensions, alignment and clearances, inspect the mould surface, profile and defects, and carry out the necessary tool tests.

Improvement｜design and troubleshooting｜Design jigs or tools according to the actual task, use CAD to assist design and investigate manufacturing equipment anomalies; the duties vary with the tool type and the role's division of work.
Section title｜Workshop precision, cooperation and working conditions

Tool and die makers often work in machining workshops and factories, both machining and assembling and inspecting. Some roles involve nights, weekends or arrangements over 40 hours, and these contexts must not be written as everyone's fixed shift system.

Common organisations and locations｜The United States BLS lists employer industries such as transportation equipment, machinery, fabricated metal products, plastics products and primary metal manufacturing. They describe the United States employment distribution and are not the recruitment proportions of Chinese enterprises; the specific workshop's equipment, temperature, ventilation and task scope need on-site confirmation.

Materials and tools of the work｜Inputs include drawings, models, technical specifications and materials; common tools cover lathes, milling machines, grinders, calipers, gauge blocks, micrometers and dial indicators. O*NET also lists CAD, CAM and ERP software categories, and a software list cannot prove that one vendor's AI functions are widely used in the role.
The process and the division of work change with new making, repair or modification tasks, and the current drawing, machining progress and assembly inspection requirements should be linked.

Scheduling and intensity｜BLS states that many roles work full time, some facilities run continuously, and nights, weekends and overtime may occur. O*NET records contexts such as standing, manual operations and noise. When job hunting, ask specifically about shifts, rest, lifting and protection conditions rather than inferring your own arrangements from the occupational title.
When explaining an anomaly, provide the object, the version, the readings and the handling record, instead of only saying "the size is a bit off" or "it feels fine".

Re-checking and the chain of responsibility｜Dimensional inspection, tool testing and repair handling all need the corresponding requirements and records. Confirm the technical responsible person before changing a critical fit or machining condition, and re-inspect the affected parts afterwards; whether mould trials, repair and final delivery are permitted must be judged by the actual authority and the organisation's process.

Quality and occupational requirements｜Quality includes whether the dimensions, alignment, clearances, surface and tool function meet the requirements, and whether the records can be traced. The United States O*NET caution, attention to detail and dependability are work style dimensions; they cannot replace supervised training, real workpieces and employer inspection.
Professional basis and boundaries of use
The precise United States occupational definition, its 18 tasks and its abilities, interests and work context.
The United States combined outlook page for this occupation and machinists; the duties and wages use the content listed separately for this occupation.
The July 2026 Xinfeng single-employer mould repair role historical sample; it supports only that role's pay and experience conditions.
The tasks and training framework of China's 2019 standard for mould workers; the application conditions must be read together with the 2023 regulations and the current local assessment requirements.
The 2023 regulations notice on the China employment website: where content is inconsistent with the current standards, the regulations prevail, and this is not an individual application approval.

Tool and die makers analyse technical specifications, calculate dimensions and tolerances, arrange materials and processes, set up and operate machine tools, and fit and assemble the related parts, making and repairing moulds, cutting tools, jigs, gauges and machined hand tools. Delivery also concerns dimensions, fit, surface and function, not just completing one machining operation.

Repairing, installing, adjusting or maintaining industrial production machinery, verifying equipment function and recording maintenance; tool making experience cannot replace whole-machine diagnostic ability.
Making, positioning, aligning and fitting structural metal product parts and delivering structural components; the assembly dimensions and process requirements need verifying against the target role.
Setting up, operating or tending forging equipment, producing formed workpieces and inspecting them; mould related experience cannot replace training on that equipment and process.
Setting up, operating or tending rolling equipment to form, thin or treat material; the focus is the rolling process and the material result, which differs from tool making.

paragraphs: New moulds and tooling
Planning the process from the drawing, machining and assembling the mould, jig or gauge, and checking the tool result by dimensions, fit and the necessary tests.
A work direction within this occupation whose goal is making the tool and its function; different tool types and process requirements cannot be swapped using one machining program.
Being willing to read drawings, calculate tolerances and arrange processes, and to link the machining, assembly and inspection evidence together.
Repair and modification
Locating an anomaly in a mould or tool, fitting and adjusting the related parts, re-inspecting and testing, and recording the changes and the unresolved items.
A task within this occupation; clarify the problem and the repair scope first, since handling one anomaly does not mean every item of the tool is acceptable.
Liking to compare the anomaly evidence and investigate fit problems, and being willing to revise the plan according to feedback rather than grinding straight away.
Industrial machinery mechanics

Moving from tool parts to whole-machine and system maintenance requires filling in equipment diagnosis, dismantling and reassembly and repair verification ability; there is no automatic transfer guarantee.
More interested in how equipment is returned to service, and willing to produce diagnosis, maintenance and functional inspection records.
Structural metal fabricators and fitters
The object changes to structural metal product parts, requiring locating, aligning, fitting and the corresponding process training for structural assembly tasks.
Being willing to work around structural component dimensions and assembly results, and to check the target site's equipment and duties.
Forging machine setters, operators and tenders
Moving from tool making to producing workpieces with forging equipment requires learning equipment setup, forming conditions and process inspection.
Preferring the production process and workpiece forming, and being able to take supervised training on the target equipment first.
Rolling machine setters, operators and tenders
Moving from tooling machining and assembly to rolled material production requires filling in equipment, material process and product dimension inspection ability.
More interested in how material changes in a continuous process, and willing to record process parameters and inspection results.
First distinguish this occupation's directions from the four adjacent occupations

New moulds and tooling, and repair and modification, are directions arranged from this occupation's tasks; industrial machinery mechanics, structural metal fabricators and fitters, forging machine setters and operators, and rolling machine setters and operators each have their own occupational objects. When choosing, compare the result you want to deliver and the ability that needs verification, and do not assume jobs are interchangeable just because they are in the same factory.

If you like making a tool step by step from a drawing, start with dimensional and process analysis; if you like finding out why a tool failed, start with anomaly location records. If the target shifts to whole-machine maintenance, structural assembly or forming production, re-check the training, environment and work output against the adjacent occupation. This is an editorial suggestion and cannot be used to predict job transfer success rates or pay increases.

The occupational directions are based on the O*NET making, repair, modification and testing tasks; the four adjacent occupations each use their own official independent definition. The suitability signals and experience order in the table are an editorial summary. The United States duty definitions cannot directly determine Chinese recruitment, qualifications or equipment operating authority, which still need checking against the role.
Once the direction is chosen, analyse whether AI support concerns process suggestions, records or actual machining verification; keep the boundaries of different tools and on-site responsibility.

At the technical ability level, Siemens publicly states that NX X Manufacturing can propose machining suggestions including operations, tools and parameters for selected geometric features; the 2606 version adds a third type of suggestion that does not depend on historical data. This proves that the vendor described a feature, not that the plan suits this factory's machine tools, fixtures and materials. Text support can be used to organise questions and records, and must still be verified against the drawing and technical requirements.

The AI support points differ for new tool making, repair and measurement records: process candidates need the equipment and machining conditions checked, repair hypotheses need the actual defect checked, and record drafts need the original readings checked. The distinctions below are an editorial analysis based on the occupational tasks and public product text, not an actual adoption survey.

Insufficient evidence: this page obtained no study of AI adoption rates, actual accuracy or net hours saved for the single occupation of tool and die making, nor Chinese deployment and wage causality data. At the adoption level, a public version feature and a product demonstration do not mean the workshop has deployed it; therefore vendor promotion is not written as widespread benefit.

The five steps below are an editorial suggestion: determine the task to be supported, check the input and permission, confirm the equipment and verification conditions, check the output manually, then save the version and results. The NIST framework provides a way to organise risk and cannot replace this factory's process, machine tool instructions or on-site safety procedures.
NIST suggests organising, measuring and managing AI risk according to the actual purpose; this page applies it as an editorial process for checking input, output and responsibility.

A pay reduction percentage cannot be inferred from an AI feature. United States wages and employment projections describe different statistical results and do not separate the effect of a single AI tool; the Chinese historical mould repair monthly wage also provides no before-and-after deployment comparison. Insufficient evidence: this page obtained no single-occupation wage study usable for this causal judgement.

After understanding the AI task boundaries, compare real job pay and requirements. Process suggestions, simulation output, on-site machining results and wage changes each need evidence, and one kind of result cannot replace another.

At the employment level, the BLS 2025—2035 table projects a 9.2% decline in employment for this occupation, with about 4,300 openings a year; it is a total projection containing many factors, not a job reduction caused by AI alone. Replacement demand does not guarantee individual hiring either, and the judgement needs checking against occupation, region, time and the actual task.

O*NET lists drawing reading, machining, assembly, measurement and testing tasks, and software categories such as CAD/CAM; this defines the task background and does not prove the effectiveness or adoption rate of generative AI.
Which step does AI change, and which result still needs verification?

Insufficient evidence: reviewable task scores, the national AI adoption rate and net employment causal results for this occupation. Vendor machining suggestions do not prove that mould making and repair testing are completed automatically; the BLS2025—2035 overall decline of 9.2%, the ten-year net reduction of about 5200 people and the average annual 4300 openings that includes replacements are component indicators and do not represent AI-only job cuts or an individual's probability of unemployment.

The five evidence cards respectively explain the occupational tasks, the risk method, the training background, the total employment and the wage basis. Vendor product cases are shown separately under market signals and the full sources; the two kinds of material do not replace one another. When reading, check the object, time and limits, then judge which conclusion it can support.
The tool making, repair and inspection tasks of United States 51-4111
The occupational tasks and software list are not an AI performance experiment or a deployment survey.
Cross-scenario AI uses, output verification and responsibility arrangements
A voluntary general framework provides no accuracy rate for this occupation and is not a Chinese on-site operating procedure.
The training, equipment and task requirements of United States tool and die makers
On-the-job training and tool inspection remain work background and cannot prove an independent effect after AI deployment.
A combined occupation page; only this occupation's explicit task and training sections are used, and no AI impact is quantified from it.
The 2025—2035 occupational total and average annual openings for United States 51-4111

2025—2035 United States 51-4111 overall decline of 9.2% and a ten-year net reduction of about 5200 people; an average of about 4300 openings a year including replacements, not a yearly net addition or a current hiring number, and not attributable to AI alone.
The total projection contains many factors and cannot be extrapolated to China, to one mould type or to individual hiring.
The coverage of United States OEWS wages and the annual／hourly statistical method
The wage statistical method distinguishes populations and units and does not measure wage changes caused by AI.
The method Q&A is not a single-occupation AI wage causality study and provides no Chinese quote.
Does a CAD/CAM software list mean generative AI is already widespread?

No. The O*NET software categories explain the occupational technical background and cannot prove that a version's AI feature has been deployed in the role; adoption evidence should also state the workshop, task, date and verification method.
Does generating a machining plan mean you can already run the machine?

No. The candidate text or parameters still need checking against the drawing, material, tooling, fixtures, machine tool and post-processing conditions, and verifying under the organisation's process. NIST only provides a risk approach, and the paper experience does not include actually running a machine.
Can real customer drawings be uploaded to a tool directly?

Check the material permission, the service settings and the retention and use scope first. An unknown tool does not automatically mean a private environment; when the permission is unclear, use the original fictional material from this page and confirm with the corresponding responsible person.
Can an AI feature directly show that wages will fall?
How many jobs in this occupation will AI reduce?

This page obtained no net job reduction figure attributable to AI alone. The BLS -9.2% is the 2025—2035 total employment change, and about 4,300 average annual openings include replacements; neither can be written directly as the number of people replaced by a tool.
Can software suggestions replace fitting and mould trial training?

This page has no research sufficient to support complete replacement. BLS and O*NET describe the machining, assembly, inspection and testing tasks, and software text alone cannot prove that a person already has these abilities or operating authority.
What is checked before the first use of a support tool?

First choose the specific task and the permitted input and state who re-checks the output; then check the drawing version, units and equipment conditions, and record the tool, version, modifications and unresolved items. If it is used in a real workshop, verify it under the organisation's existing process.

Insufficient evidence: the national wage distribution for tool and die makers in mainland China. The pre-tax annual average of 80,739 yuan for production, manufacturing and related personnel in enterprises above the designated size in 2025 covers many categories of personnel including basic machining for machinery manufacturing and metal products manufacturing; it is used as a broad reference for tool machining and assembly tasks, not a separately listed wage, median, starting pay or personal range for this occupation.

When discussing pay, check the wage composition, the actual shift system, overtime, probation and settlement arrangements. The historical posting disclosed only a monthly wage range, and which parts are fixed wage, bonus or overtime income still needs confirming.

Check cash wages, social insurance, board and lodging and other benefits separately. The posting lists company level five insurances and the housing fund and benefits such as board and lodging, but a benefit list cannot be used to infer the post-tax amount received or an individual's disposable income.

In the July 24, 2026 Xinfeng historical posting, Jiangxi Minglida Technology Co., Ltd. sought 5 mould repair masters, disclosing 8,000—11,000 yuan per month. It required at least 5 years of relevant experience in large die casting or plastic mould making, and the ability to read 2D/3D drawings, among others; whether it is still open has not been verified.

That monthly wage applies only to the historical quote for the Xinfeng single-employer mould repair master role. The row does not state pre-tax or post-tax, the wage components or the full shift system; the conditions of general workers, CNC or quality inspection roles in the same posting must not be borrowed, and it must not be treated as starting pay for a beginner.
China pay: official broad production roles, the Xinfeng mould repair historical sample and the occupational gap
Historical single-employer mould repair role: 8,000—11,000 yuan per month; the tax basis, wage components and current open status have not been verified.

Insufficient evidence: no quote on the same basis was obtained for entry-level beginners, new tooling roles and national occupational wages. The experienced mould repair role cannot be used to fill in those figures, and 5 recruitment places cannot be counted as 5 employers.

The sample requires at least 5 years of relevant mould making experience and drawing reading, process and equipment ability; it is a single-role requirement, not a uniform number of years for all mould roles.

The job conditions and pay of the entry direction still need to be read from postings separately; the paper practice can only show your thinking and cannot prove that you meet the requirements for an experienced mould repair master.
The work content of making new moulds, jigs or gauges exists according to the occupational tasks, but no comparable current Chinese wage sample was obtained this time.

1 employer, 1 role and 5 places is historical recruitment material and does not constitute a national wage sample. Tool type, region, experience and shift system are not controlled, so no national high or low wage ranking can be based on it.

Continuous paid arrangements and overtime conditions affect personal income. Check the contract and the current role first, rather than multiplying the historical range by 12 or converting a United States percentile into a Chinese monthly wage.

Insufficient evidence: the process suggestion capability of an AI product cannot directly show that Chinese mould repair wages will fall. Evidence of actual deployment, task division, output and pay changes is needed; this page obtained no Chinese AI adoption rate or wage causality data for this occupation. When comparing specific roles, still separate the fixed wage, overtime, bonus, shift system and equipment task scope.

The 2025 pre-tax annual average of 80,739 yuan for broad production and manufacturing roles in enterprises above the designated size is not a separately listed distribution for tool and die making. The Xinfeng 2026-07-24 single-employer experienced mould repair figure of 8000—11000 yuan per month is a historical quote whose tax basis, components, hours and current open status are unchecked, and the two are not combined into personal upper and lower limits; the precise national distribution is still missing, and United States wages or other roles in the same posting are not used to fill in the pay.

The 2025 United States median wage for tool and die makers is 64,050 US dollars per year and 30.79 US dollars per hour. The official national 51-4111 row is used; a statistical wage is not an individual's post-tax amount received, fixed hours or a hiring offer.
P10 is 44,680 US dollars per year and 21.48 US dollars per hour, describing the lower part of the national wage distribution; it must not be treated as a beginner's wage or a minimum pay commitment.

P90 is 92,680 US dollars per year and 44.56 US dollars per hour, describing the higher part of the national wage distribution; it cannot be inferred that it is a senior level or that an individual can obtain the same income continuously.

BLS projects employment in this occupation falling from about 56,700 in 2025 to about 51,500 in 2035, a change of -9.2% and a net reduction of about 5,200 people; about 4,300 openings a year including replacements cannot be mixed up with annual net growth.

OEWS wage data exclude the self-employed, while the employment projection and the wage survey have different coverage; self-employment business receipts or total occupational income cannot be estimated from them.

The official tables list annual and hourly wages together; the standard OEWS work year is usually statistically converted at 2,080 hours. This page adopts both units directly from the original tables, and where an individual's hours, bonuses and taxes are unknown, no monthly wage or actual annual income is derived.
United States wages: national percentiles kept separate from actual pay
The 2025 national wage distribution for the United States

The median is the middle position of the national statistical population and does not represent a uniform seniority or working arrangement; both the annual and hourly values come from the same official national row.
How should this set of annual and hourly wages be compared?

P10, P25, P50, P75 and P90 are positions in the same occupational wage distribution. Years of service and job requirements do not correspond one to one with each percentile, so P25 cannot be written directly as an apprentice and P75 as a senior worker. Personal pay also needs checking against the tasks and the actual pay conditions.

When comparing offers, unify the units first, then check the work location, tool type, scope of responsibility, shift system, overtime and bonus composition. Wage percentiles, industry medians and employer offers answer different questions, and a direction must not be chosen on one figure alone.
The median annual wage for this occupation in three manufacturing industries

values: E1 material｜locating pin dimension check

This page is an original fictional paper prompt and does not represent a real drawing or process. Fixture locating pin drawing version A: diameter 10.00±0.02 millimetres, with both limits included. The same fictional instrument G7 is given as within the prompt-given validity period and the inspection conditions meet the prompt; the three readings are R1=9.985, R2=10.018 and R3=10.024 millimetres.

The artificial practice rule: only when the original value falls within the closed interval [lower limit, upper limit] and the prompt-given inspection conditions are valid may you write "paper dimensions conform". Do not round first; a value out of range is written as "paper out of tolerance"; invalid conditions are written as "awaiting valid re-measurement". No mating hole, assembly clearance or functional test material is provided, so the fixture as a whole or the physical item cannot be judged releasable.
E2 feedback｜version and inspection condition change

Switch to drawing version B: diameter 10.00±0.01 millimetres, with both limits included. Only in this paper prompt is it permitted to use the three old E1 readings as a numerical comparison against the new version, not as an on-site re-measurement. The added R4=10.006 millimetres is covered by the prompt-given G7 and the conditions are valid; for R5=10.000 millimetres, the prompt-given instrument G9 has passed its validity period.

Task: complete E1 first, then keep the old conclusion and make the E2 comparison, calculate the limits for both versions, and explain the value position and the inspection validity item by item. Write two questions awaiting confirmation: how do we obtain a valid re-measurement record for R5? How do we complete the assembly and functional acceptance basis? Do not operate equipment, and do not assume a hole diameter or a new acceptance standard.
Reference answer｜dimensions and validity kept separate

Version A interval [9.98,10.02] millimetres: the paper dimensions of R1 and R2 conform, and R3 exceeds 10.02. Version B interval [9.99,10.01]: in the numerical comparison of the old readings, R1 is below the lower limit and R2 and R3 are above the upper limit; R4 is within range and the prompt-given conditions are valid, so it is recorded as conforming on paper. R5 is within range but the inspection conditions are invalid, so it is recorded as awaiting valid re-measurement.

The two conforming conclusions for version A cannot be carried over to version B. The conformity of R4 and the pending re-measurement of R5 also cannot be used to infer that the fixture as a whole passes acceptance; the hole, clearance and functional material are still missing. The piece keeps the original readings, the drawing version, the conditions, the judgements and the reasons for revision, and states that all material is fictional and that no real machining or inspection took place.
Practice boundaries｜not a physical release

The prompt's validity period and closed interval are artificially simplified conditions and do not simulate complete measurement uncertainty, instrument calibration or real acceptance rules. Only paper calculation and recording; do not start machine tools, grind, weld, lift or run mould trials, do not use customer drawings, and do not treat the answers as actual machining and release instructions.

description.text: Tool and die makers calculate dimensions and tolerances from drawings and technical requirements, arrange machining processes, and make and repair moulds, cutting tools, jigs and gauges. The work includes both machine tool machining and assembly, measurement and testing; the delivery standard is whether the tool works as required, not merely whether the parts have been machined.
